title: By the winds sent out, one gust after another.
subtitle: Why the surah swears by the wind
then: Ibn Masud reported this surah was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ {idea}in a cave at Mina{/idea}, and he learned it fresh from his mouth. Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas and others said the "ones sent forth" are {idea}the winds{/idea}; some said angels. Umm al-Fadl said it was {reward}the last thing she heard him recite, in the Maghrib prayer.{/reward}
now: A breeze through the window on a hot night. You barely notice it. {idea}The word used here is "sent."{/idea} Every gust is dispatched, like a message, by the One who also promised the Day.
old: The wind is just air moving around.
new: Even the wind is sent. Nothing in the world is purposeless.
try: Next time you feel a breeze, say SubhanAllah and remember it was sent.

title: And by the winds that blow with violent force.
subtitle: The same air, now a storm
then: Ibn Jarir affirmed that these {trap}are the winds{/trap}; Arabs said winds 'asafat {trap}when they roar with their blowing.{/trap} {idea}The One who sends a breeze can send a storm.{/idea}
now: A storm warning on your phone. Trees bending, power out, you sitting in the dark with candles. {idea}You feel how small you are.{/idea} The same power will bring the Day.
new: The power behind a storm is the power behind the Day.
try: During the next strong wind, make a short dua for safety and mercy.

title: And by the winds that spread the clouds.
subtitle: Winds that carry mercy
then: Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}winds that scatter clouds across the sky{/idea} by Allah's will; Abu Salih said it is the rain. He cites the verse: {reward}He sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy.{/reward}
now: Clouds gather after a dry month. Farmers watch the sky, you watch the forecast. {reward}The wind that brings them is part of a system built for you.{/reward}
old: Rain just happens when it happens.
new: The winds carry rain by design. Mercy is sent before it arrives.
try: When it next rains, make a dua. Rain is a time of mercy.

title: And by the angels who separate truth from falsehood.
subtitle: The ones who bring the dividing line
then: Ibn Kathir says here there is {idea}no difference of opinion: these are the angels.{/idea} They descend with Allah's command to the messengers, {idea}separating truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, lawful from forbidden.{/idea}
now: Everything online is blurred: opinions, hot takes, "it depends." You lose the sense of what is actually right. {idea}The revelation is the line that does not blur.{/idea}
old: Right and wrong are mostly up to each person.
new: Allah sent a clear line through His angels. I can find it.
try: When you are unsure about something today, check what the Quran says first.

title: And by the angels who deliver the reminder.
subtitle: Revelation reaching the messengers
then: Ibn Kathir says the angels {idea}bring the revelation to the messengers.{/idea} It is called dhikr, a reminder. {reward}It was carried with care, all the way down to you.{/reward}
now: You get dozens of reminders a day: meetings, bills, birthdays. You tap them away. {idea}This one was delivered by angels.{/idea} It deserves more than a swipe.
old: The Quran is one more thing on my list.
new: The Quran is a reminder Allah sent through angels, meant for me.
try: Set one phone reminder today that is only for reading a few verses.

title: To excuse some, and to warn others.
subtitle: Two purposes of the message
then: Ibn Kathir says the revelation contains {reward}exemption or absolvement for the creatures{/reward} and {trap}a warning of Allah's torment if they oppose His command.{/trap} {idea}It opens a door and marks a cliff edge.{/idea}
now: A doctor tells you your blood sugar is high. It sounds like bad news. But it is also the moment you can still fix it. {reward}A warning in time is a gift.{/reward}
old: Religious warnings are just there to scare me.
new: A warning comes with an excuse attached: a way to be cleared.
try: Read one warning verse today and ask: what way out does it offer me?

title: What you are promised will surely happen.
subtitle: The point of all five oaths
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}this is the subject of the oaths.{/idea} The Hour, the horn, the raising of bodies, the gathering of first and last, {reward}and every doer repaid for his deed: good for good, evil for evil.{/reward} {idea}It will come to pass.{/idea}
now: You make promises you mean to keep: I will call, I will pay you back, I will be there. Some slip. {idea}This promise does not slip.{/idea}
old: The Day might happen. Who knows?
new: It will happen. Winds and angels are sworn by to make that clear.
try: Do one good deed today with the promise of repayment in mind.

title: When the stars are wiped out.
subtitle: The lights that guided travelers go dark
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}their light will leave{/trap}, comparing it to the verses about stars falling and scattering. In Makkah, people {idea}navigated deserts by these stars.{/idea}
now: You go camping and see the night sky without city lights. Thousands of stars, ancient and steady. {idea}Even they will go out.{/idea} The promise of the Day is steadier than they are.
old: The stars will be there long after me.
new: The stars have an end. What Allah promised does not.
try: Look up at the night sky tonight for one minute and remember this verse.

title: When the sky is split open.
subtitle: The roof over the world cracks
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {trap}cleft asunder, its sides fall and its edges become weak.{/trap} The sky that looked like the most solid thing {idea}opens like a cracked shell.{/idea}
now: You look up on a blue afternoon and the sky feels like a ceiling that will always hold. {idea}This verse says it will crack.{/idea} What are you building under it?
old: The sky is the most permanent thing there is.
new: Even the sky will open. Only what I do for Allah stays.
try: Do one thing today that will still matter when the sky splits.

title: When the mountains are blown away like dust.
subtitle: No trace of them left
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will be removed and no sight or trace of them will remain.{/trap} He cites the verse where {idea}the earth becomes a level plain and all people are gathered, none left behind.{/idea}
now: You drive past the mountains on a family trip. They were there when your grandparents were young. {idea}They will be gone.{/idea} So will every big problem that feels like a mountain to you today.
old: My problems are like mountains: huge and fixed.
new: Even mountains will be dust. My problems are smaller than they look.
try: Name one worry that feels like a mountain, and hand it to Allah in dua.

title: When the messengers are gathered at their appointed time.
subtitle: The witnesses called forward
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}gathered{/idea}; Mujahid said {idea}postponed{/idea}; Ibrahim said {idea}promised.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse where {reward}the Prophets and witnesses are brought forward and judgment is given with truth.{/reward}
now: You read about the prophets as stories for children. Nuh, Musa, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ. {idea}They will be present that Day, as witnesses to whether the message was heard.{/idea}
old: The prophets are figures from the past.
new: The messengers will be gathered to testify. Their message is for me now.
try: Send salawat on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today.

title: For which Day was all this delayed?
subtitle: A question to make you lean in
then: Ibn Kathir says: {idea}for which Day are the messengers postponed and their matter awaited, until the Hour is established?{/idea} He cites: {reward}do not think Allah will fail to keep His promise to His messengers.{/reward}
now: A trial date keeps being moved. The other side starts acting like it will never happen. {idea}Delay is not cancellation.{/idea}
old: If it has not happened yet, it probably will not.
new: It is delayed to a set Day. The delay is time given to me.
try: Use one delayed thing today, a free hour, as time to prepare.

title: For the Day of Sorting.
subtitle: The Day everyone is separated
then: The answer to the question: {idea}the Day of Sorting Out{/idea}, the Day when the people of Paradise are separated from the people of the Fire. Ibn Kathir calls it {idea}the Day when it is judged between them with truth.{/idea}
now: At work, at school, in the mall, everyone is mixed: honest and dishonest, kind and cruel, all in the same queue. {idea}One Day the queues split.{/idea}
old: In the end, everyone ends up in the same place.
new: There is a Day of sorting, and I am choosing my line now.
try: Do one thing today that belongs in the line you want to stand in.

title: And what will make you know what that Day is?
subtitle: Too big to imagine
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah asks this {idea}to magnify its matter.{/idea} The listeners in Makkah had demanded the Day as a joke. {trap}The question tells them they have no idea what they are asking for.{/trap}
now: You hear about the Day of Judgement so often it sounds normal, like a weather report. {idea}This verse stops you: you do not actually know what it is.{/idea}
old: I have heard enough about the Day already.
new: Whatever I think the Day is, it is bigger.
try: Sit for one quiet minute today and just think about standing before Allah.

title: Woe, that Day, to those who denied it was coming.
subtitle: The first refrain: after the Day of Sorting
then: This is the first of ten times this line comes. Here it follows {idea}the Day of Sorting and the undoing of the sky{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}woe to them from Allah's torment that is coming.{/trap} The surah introduction says Makkah's people had demanded the Day as a joke.
now: Someone mocks the idea of judgement on a podcast and the room laughs. You laugh along so you do not look strange. {idea}This verse asks where you will stand when the joke is over.{/idea}
old: Joking about the Day is harmless.
new: Denying the Day, even laughing it off, is something I do not want to be part of.
try: Next time the Day is mocked around you, do not laugh along.
